pages.title: Mistral raises €3B to make sovereign, open-weight AI the technology frontier
pages.what_its_about: European AI startup Mistral has raised a €3 billion Series D funding round at a valuation of over €21 billion.
key_points: Led by Samsung Electronics, Mistral secured €3 billion in Series D funding—the largest ever for a European technology company—achieving a post-money valuation of over €21 billion.
The raised capital will be allocated toward expanding frontier AI research, scaling compute capacity for training powerful models, and expanding its global commercial presence.
Through a full-stack approach combining open-weight models and infrastructure, it provides enterprises and public institutions with a sovereign AI environment free from vendor lock-in.
notable_data_or_quotes: Series D funding amount: €3 billion
Valuation: post-money valuation of more than €21 billion
Time since founding: Achieved the largest private funding round in European tech company history in just 3 years
Operational scale: Supporting more than 125 global enterprises across 20 countries, including Airbus, ASML, and HSBC
Key investors: Samsung Electronics (Lead), Scaleup Europe Fund (EQT), PSG Equity, Advent, funds managed by BlackRock, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, etc.
pages.intended_audience: AI industry investors, global enterprise IT decision-makers, and business leaders

pages.title: Hallo, Deutschland!
pages.what_its_about: French AI company Mistral is establishing a new hub in Munich, Germany, Europe's largest industrial powerhouse, accelerating its expansion into industrial and physics AI.
key_points: Mistral has opened a Munich hub and deployed a dedicated research team for Physics AI and industrial AI to support key German industries such as automotive, energy, and manufacturing.
The company is collaborating with BMW on crash simulations and with Siemens Energy on developing industrial AI applications, having absorbed physics specialists from Emmi AI, acquired in May 2026.
To secure European AI sovereignty, Mistral plans to build 1 GW of European compute capacity by 2030 and offer data security and auditability within customer infrastructure through open-weight models.
notable_data_or_quotes: To secure Europe’s AI sovereignty, Mistral will build one gigawatt of European compute capacity by 2030.
Following our acquisition of Emmi AI in May 2026, more than 30 physicists, researchers, and engineers with unique expertise in Physics and Engineering AI joined Mistral.
Dr. Karsten Wildberger: "Mistral is a powerful example of what Europe can achieve: developing cutting-edge technology, turning it into a global success, and taking responsibility at the same time."
pages.intended_audience: European and global manufacturing and industrial enterprise leaders, AI researchers, and policymakers

pages.title: Mistral and Mozilla are bringing open, private and multilingual AI to your web browser
pages.what_its_about: Mistral and Mozilla have partnered to integrate Mistral's open, multilingual AI models into Firefox Smart Window, Mozilla's web browsing AI assistant.
key_points: Mozilla's AI browsing assistant, 'Firefox Smart Window (beta)', is powered by Mistral models to support complex search organization and tab-based information exploration.
It will initially be available to users in France and North America, with support expanding to the United Kingdom and Germany later this year.
It provides customized AI tailored to local languages and cultural contexts, with privacy protections applied by default, such as unsaved conversations and a zero data retention policy.
notable_data_or_quotes: Firefox Smart Window (beta), Mozilla’s AI browsing assistant, is now powered by Mistral models.
Mistral will help power Smart Window for users in France and North America, with the United Kingdom and Germany expected to follow later this year.
conversations aren’t saved on Mozilla’s servers by default, and partners like Mistral agree to zero data retention.
pages.intended_audience: Firefox browser users, the general public, and IT professionals interested in privacy-focused AI web search tools

pages.title: Cloudera and Mistral Partner to Bring Specialized, Sovereign Intelligence to Enterprise Data
pages.what_its_about: Mistral and Cloudera have partnered to enable enterprises to build customized and sovereign AI while maintaining full control over their data in their own environments.
key_points: Mistral models are integrated with Cloudera's hybrid data platform, enabling inference to run on their own infrastructure, including on-premises, public/private cloud, and fully air-gapped environments.

Enables enterprises in regulated industries (finance, manufacturing, telecommunications, etc.) to leverage decades of accumulated proprietary data to train and build customized AI models while retaining data ownership.

Implements Sovereign AI by keeping data, intelligence, compute, and operations under customer control, enabling enterprises to transition from 'renting generic AI' to 'owning intelligence that is uniquely theirs'.
notable_data_or_quotes: "Every enterprise is heading toward the same destination: specialized intelligence... from renting generic AI to owning intelligence that’s uniquely theirs." — Abhas Ricky, Chief Business Officer & GM, Applied AI at Cloudera

"It’s a privilege to have the opportunity to bring Mistral’s sovereign AI to Cloudera’s 30 exabytes of customer-managed data running on its platform." — Kamal Brar, SVP of Partnerships & Alliances at Mistral
30 exabytes

pages.title: Modernizing complex legacy code with AI agents.
pages.what_its_about: Introduces a case study and key methodologies for successfully migrating 40,000 lines of complex legacy Fortran 77 code to a modern C++ system using AI agents.
key_points: Conducted a project to convert a 40,000-line physics-based reservoir simulator, which lacked test suites and centralized documentation, into C++.
Key success factors included establishing an equivalence testing framework to verify numerical consistency, pre-documenting code with AI agents, and balancing human review with agent autonomy.

Beyond simple syntax translation, refactored the architecture from a procedural global memory (COMMON blocks) structure to object-oriented C++ and modern scientific computing frameworks such as PETSc.

Fortran 77

pages.intended_audience: Software engineers, developers responsible for legacy system modernization and scientific computing, and technical leaders interested in adopting AI coding agents.

pages.title: Splice CEO Kakul Srivastava thinks AI emails are killing conversations
pages.what_its_about: An interview in which Kakul Srivastava, CEO of music sample platform Splice, expresses concerns that AI-generated documents and tools could undermine human-centered genuine communication and creative processes.
key_points: Splice avoids one-click music generation methods (such as Suno) and aims to adopt AI tools that place human creators at the center.
CEO Kakul Srivastava pointed out that AI-written documents and emails hinder deep thinking and genuine conversation among team members.
She emphasized the importance of conversations carrying human intent and deliberation in remote-first work environments, noting that the same principle applies to music creation.

pages.title: An OpenAI safety employee has quit and is sounding the alarm
pages.what_its_about: An OpenAI employee who wrote safety reports has resigned, criticizing the AI industry's safety culture as fundamentally broken.
key_points: David Robinson, who wrote safety reports for major models at OpenAI, resigned and publicly criticized the industry's culture in a piece for The Atlantic.

He argued that Silicon Valley is overly focused on excessive optimism and a race for speed while overlooking potential risks, claiming AI companies require the safeguards and caution of nuclear power plants.
Recently, there has been a wave of departures and public warnings from safety researchers at major AI companies, including Anthropic and Google DeepMind.
notable_data_or_quotes: "Given today’s risks, frontier labs need to run like nuclear power plants or busy airports, with layers of redundancy and careful, time-consuming planning, so that the occasional and inevitable human error does not open a door to disaster."
Jacob Coxon: AI "could kill us all by the end of the decade."
pages.intended_audience: The general public and industry professionals interested in AI safety, corporate ethics, and regulatory policy

pages.title: Reverse Item Response Theory for Sparsity-Robust Ranking in Fragmented Cancer Drug-Response Matrices
pages.what_its_about: A study on robust rank prediction that applies reverse Item Response Theory to address missing data issues in cancer cell drug-response matrices.
key_points: Introduced reverse Item Response Theory (reverse IRT) into pharmacogenomics by modeling cancer types as 'examinees' with resistance capacity and drugs as 'items' with evasion difficulty.
Applied to 242,036 measurements from the GDSC2 database, achieving higher rank recovery compared to simple averages (Delta-rho = +0.089 to +0.095) and optimal Brier scores even under 60% missingness.
Demonstrated 82% directional agreement in cross-validation on the PRISM dataset, proving methodological evaluation robustness in fragmented data settings.

GDSC2
Delta-rho = +0.089 to +0.095 at 60% missingness
19 of 28 cancer types

pages.intended_audience: Bioinformatics and computational biology researchers, drug discovery pharmacogenomics research teams, and machine learning-based healthcare data analysts

pages.title: How Far is Adam from Natural Gradient Descent?
pages.what_its_about: This study analyzes how geometrically aligned Adam, the standard optimization algorithm in deep learning, is with Natural Gradient Descent (NGD) and identifies the actual factors behind its success.
key_points: Analyzed Adam's full update rule, including momentum, from the perspective of diagonal empirical Fisher information approximation and measured its geometric deviation from NGD across four loss landscapes.

While deviations were small under well-conditioned settings, they reached approximately 10^3 in ill-conditioned settings and neural networks, and geometric drift did not adversely affect final loss minimization even if it slowed initial convergence.
Demonstrated that Adam's superior optimization performance does not stem from closely tracking the NGD trajectory, but from the balance between structural approximation error and momentum smoothing.
notable_data_or_quotes: \approx 10^3
\gamma(\Delta\theta)
pages.intended_audience: Machine learning optimization theory researchers and deep learning algorithm developers

pages.title: FourierQK: Filter Shape, Admissibility and the Leakage-Coverage Law
pages.what_its_about: This study analyzes the optimal filter shape and spectral leakage-coverage characteristics of FourierQK, which applies band-pass filters instead of Q/K dot products in attention mechanisms.
key_points: Confirmed that suppression of DC and Nyquist components and an oscillatory band-pass structure are essential.
Achieved a +1.15 nats performance improvement over standard dot-product attention at a single-scale bandwidth (sigma ~= 2 bins) centered around the paragraph level (~70 tokens).
Demonstrated that an admissible filter (Mexican Hat DOG m = 2) outperforms Gaussian filters and partially prevents bidirectional FFT leakage.

pages.title: Fast Polynomial Transcendentals for LLMs
pages.what_its_about: A study that improves LLM training speed by applying polynomial approximations to resolve bottlenecks in special function operations on modern GPUs such as NVIDIA Blackwell.
key_points: Replaced native PyTorch operations with FMA-based 3rd to 4th-degree polynomial programs to alleviate Special Function Unit (SFU) bottlenecks resulting from GPU architecture evolution.

Achieved overall training throughput improvements ranging from 0.3% up to 8.0% across four integration tasks (dense SiLU, tanh-softcapped attention, sigmoid attention, and routed-expert SwiGLU) in a GB200 environment.
At approximately 100 billion tokens of training, the final smoothed training loss difference compared to native operations remained between -0.107 and +0.079, stably preserving model performance.
notable_data_or_quotes: 1.19x to 2.19x performance improvement when resident in L2 and 1.00x to 1.70x when resident in HBM in isolated paths
Full training step throughput improved by 2.7%, 2.9%, and 8.0% when replacing dense-SiLU, tanh-softcapped-attention, and routed-expert, respectively
7.4% improvement in full attention forward pass and 0.3% improvement in overall GPU step when replacing sigmoid-attention
Final training loss difference (polynomial minus native) of -0.107 to +0.079 at the 100 billion tokens scale
pages.intended_audience: AI systems engineers, GPU kernel optimization researchers, LLM distributed training developers

pages.title: SW-KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks with Stieltjes-Wigert q-Orthogonal Polynomials
pages.what_its_about: This study proposes a novel Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (SW-KAN) architecture that introduces Stieltjes-Wigert q-orthogonal polynomials to address the domain mismatch problem between unbounded real-valued inputs and orthogonal polynomial bases.
key_points: It adopts Stieltjes-Wigert q-orthogonal polynomials defined on the semi-infinite interval (0, infinity) and stably bridges the domain gap via a smooth exponential-of-tanh mapping while maintaining favorable gradient conditioning.
It achieves computational efficiency by utilizing a numerically stable three-term recurrence relation that evaluates polynomial expansions in O(N) operations without requiring special function calls.

By providing inductive bias through a log-normal weight structure and learnable q-parameters, it demonstrates superior expressiveness and an improved accuracy-efficiency trade-off compared to existing polynomial KANs, even in resource-constrained settings such as dimensionality reduction or data scarcity.
notable_data_or_quotes: (0, infinity)
O(N)
pages.intended_audience: AI and machine learning researchers and engineers interested in deep learning architectures, neural network-based function approximation, and resource-efficient model design.

pages.title: The Four Horsemen of Agentic Coding
pages.what_its_about: An article analyzing the adverse effects lurking behind the utility of agent-based coding: slop, alienation from work, deskilling, and the erosion of social bonds within teams.
key_points: Due to the characteristic style generated by LLMs (slop), code that humans are reluctant to read proliferates, creating a risk of turning codebases into wastelands.
Directing and reviewing agents instead of coding directly increases psychological distance from the work, weakening sense of ownership, craftsmanship, and affection for software.
Reliance on AI tools reduces incentives to maintain development capabilities and learn anew, while shrinking opportunities for peer inquiries and mutual recognition, eroding team cohesion.
notable_data_or_quotes: Four issues: slop, alienation, deskilling, and the weakening of team relationships
A shared space where everyone once contributed turns into an AI wasteland where humans do not want to spend time
Today's high productivity relies on a unique situation where developers who became proficient through years of hands-on work skillfully leverage LLMs
pages.intended_audience: Software engineers, tech leads, engineering managers, and organizations adopting AI coding tools

ADR Writer records the rationale and constraints behind design decisions to support implementation, code reviews, and consistency verification between documentation and code.
Even if the plugins are removed, generated documents and code are preserved in the repository, and they operate in Claude Code and Codex environments on Node.js 24 or higher.

pages.title: ds4: From DeepSeek-Exclusive to a Local Inference Engine That Also Runs Qwen and GLM
pages.what_its_about: DwarfStar 4 (ds4), a C-based local inference engine, expands its support beyond DeepSeek to include Qwen and GLM models, providing a high-performance local inference and coding agent integration environment.
key_points: An MIT-licensed inference engine supporting Mac, CUDA, and ROCm environments, applying asymmetric 2-bit quantization technology to efficiently run large-scale MoE models on local machines.
Three interfaces—CLI, local HTTP API, and native coding agent—share model state and cache, while SSD-based long prefix caching optimizes the prefill process upon restarts.
Provides OpenAI- and Anthropic-style API compatibility, allowing seamless connection of various coding agents such as Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode to the local server.

pages.title: What’s next after Jev? Metacache: Reasoning by Construction [D]
pages.what_its_about: This article proposes Metacache, a reasoning framework that shifts away from single monolithic models to build and reuse compound systems combining small agents with code orchestration.
key_points: To address the unpredictability and difficulty of modifying monolithic models, the paradigm is shifting toward compound systems that combine small agents with a code-based orchestration layer.

Instead of having the model answer directly, it proposes an approach where the model constructs and executes a compound system (reasonlet) composed of small agents, returning both the result and the system itself.
The returned reasonlet can be stored locally for repeated execution and modification without recalling the model, or cached on the provider side (metacache) to save computational resources.
notable_data_or_quotes: A monolithic model is unpredictable and hard to change, but it programs itself during training. Code is the opposite – it is predictable and easy to change, but it must be written explicitly.
A saved, reusable reasonlet is a metacache.
pages.intended_audience: AI system architects, machine learning researchers, and LLM application developers

pages.title: iPhone 18 Pro Max can’t call or text on AT&T? Apple will replace it for free
pages.what_its_about: Apple is providing free device replacements after some iPhone 18 Pro Max units on the AT&T network experienced dropped calls and lost data connectivity.
key_points: Issues have been reported where some iPhone 18 Pro Max units on the AT&T network lose cellular service, leaving users unable to make calls, send texts (including to 911), or use mobile data.

Apple rolled out iOS 27.0.1 and a carrier settings update as preventive measures, but units that have already experienced connectivity failures cannot be restored via software, prompting Apple to offer free hardware replacements.

Although the exact cause has not been officially announced, teardown analyses by iFixit and TechInsights suggest a possible link to cellular hardware components, such as a new millimeter-wave (mmWave) antenna.
notable_data_or_quotes: "We released iOS 27.0.1 earlier this week and strongly encourage all iPhone 18 Pro Max users to update now, and are also issuing a carrier settings update today."
"Some phones may be unable to complete calls/text/data, including to 911"

pages.title: 'AI Backlash' Masked by Cute Characters... Alexandr Wang Drives Hit Success of 'Muse'
pages.what_its_about: Big tech companies are actively adopting friendly mascots and consumer-friendly marketing strategies to alleviate public resistance and anxiety toward AI and expand their user base.
key_points: Under the leadership of 29-year-old CAIO Alexandr Wang, Meta propelled its AI personal assistant app 'Muse' to No. 1 on the App Store using the mascot 'Jolly' and unconventional meme marketing.
Major AI companies such as OpenAI ('Dots') and Anthropic ('Claude') are also utilizing character mascots and merchandise to lower technological apprehension and cultivate an approachable image.

Rather than getting caught up in technical rivalries or regulatory debates, Meta is focusing on acquiring mainstream active users by highlighting everyday shopping and payment partnerships alongside an intuitive user experience (UX).
notable_data_or_quotes: The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) survey of 1,300 consumers: More than half of respondents view AI as a societal existential threat, and approximately 70% express concern over job loss
Allen Adamson: "Fear of AI is growing by the day, but it's hard to be afraid of something cute."
Cheryl Berman: "Characters become brands that turn abstract technology into something familiar."

Nate Weiner: "Meta's current strategy is to let Anthropic and OpenAI take on the risks of AI and regulatory debates, while targeting general consumers who want everyday tools like email management and shopping."
pages.intended_audience: General readers and business professionals interested in big tech marketing strategies and trends in the mainstream adoption of AI services

pages.title: Bubbleshare Unveils AI Search Performance Analytics Solution: 'Accurate Citations Are Key, Rather Than Mere Exposure'
pages.what_its_about: Bubbleshare has unveiled 'VIVI', an AI search visibility solution that goes beyond mere exposure to support accurate brand citations within AI responses and content improvements across each stage of the buyer's journey.
key_points: The solution 'VIVI' diagnoses the mention and citation status of brands and competitors across major AI search environments—such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity—into four stages: presence, exposure opportunity, actual mention, and source citation.

Going beyond simply assessing average exposure rates, it designs question sets tailored to customer intent and the buyer's journey—such as information exploration, alternative comparison, and purchase decisions—to conduct in-depth analysis.
After analyzing underperforming prompts and content gaps, it provides integrated support ranging from specific draft content improvements to marketing action plans.
notable_data_or_quotes: The key lies not in a tool that merely checks visibility in AI search, but in an operational foundation that connects AI search visibility to content actions and performance validation.

While conventional search engine optimization (SEO) tools focus on search rankings, keyword traffic, backlinks, and page performance, Bubbleshare examines how brands are understood within AI responses.
Bubbleshare will host its first webinar on the upcoming 30th at 4:00 PM to share real-world case studies on diagnosing and improving brand content in AI search environments.
Founded in 2023
pages.intended_audience: Corporate marketers, brand managers, SEO specialists, and content planners

pages.title: Apple Tightens macOS 'Full Disk Access' Controls Amid Rising Unauthorized Access by AI Agents
pages.what_its_about: Apple is strengthening macOS 'Full Disk Access' permission controls to reduce privacy breach risks arising from data access by desktop AI agents.
key_points: Apple announced the introduction of additional controls, such as explicit approval procedures, to macOS 'Full Disk Access' permissions to prevent unauthorized data access and security risks from AI agents.
Taking preemptive action, Apple pointed out that broad permissions designed for backups could recently be exploited by AI agents or expose the private data of conversation partners.
This move comes in response to growing concerns over data misuse by desktop AI agents, including OpenAI's ChatGPT Messages integration and controversies over privacy access by Meta's AI agent Muse.
notable_data_or_quotes: Apple announced on the 2nd (local time) that it plans to introduce additional controls to macOS 'Full Disk Access' permissions.
Apple: "As AI agents become increasingly active and autonomous, the security risks posed by broad permissions such as Full Disk Access are also growing significantly."
Last August, OpenAI added an optional feature to ChatGPT for Mac that allows it to read and summarize conversations from Apple's Messages app or compose and send messages on behalf of the user.
pages.intended_audience: macOS users, Mac app and AI agent developers, information security and IT administrators

pages.title: Chinese AI Infiltrates South Korean Enterprises... Warning Lights on 'Model Lock-in'
pages.what_its_about: As South Korean companies increasingly adopt Chinese open-weight AI models such as Alibaba's Qwen, concerns are growing over dependency on specific models and the burden of switching costs resulting from potential future licensing policy changes.
key_points: A growing number of South Korean enterprises are adopting Chinese open-weight AI models like Alibaba's Qwen on their internal servers, driven by cost savings and strong Korean language performance.

While Qwen-derived models and Hugging Face download shares have surged, tight integration with internal enterprise systems raises concerns over 'model lock-in,' making future migration to alternative models difficult.

Risks surrounding licensing changes in future versions are escalating, as seen in latest large models like Qwen 3.8 Max requiring a separate commercial license agreement for companies exceeding a specific revenue threshold.
notable_data_or_quotes: Kim Hyun-joo, Director at the Korea Artificial Intelligence & Software Industry Association (KOSA): "More South Korean companies are utilizing Chinese open-weight models," adding, "Qwen, in particular, is considered to have relatively high Korean language comprehension, leading to frequent enterprise adoption."
In an evaluation by the National Institute of Korean Language, the Qwen series scored 2.18 points on Korean language tasks, closely trailing Naver HyperCLOVA X (2.22 points).

According to Hugging Face, the Qwen series logged approximately 2.061 billion downloads and 151,448 derivative models between January and July this year (2.6 times the total of Meta, 4.7 times that of the Llama series).
Qwen 3.8 Max requires a separate commercial license agreement for enterprises whose combined revenue over the previous 12 months exceeds $50 million (approx. 67.3 billion KRW).
pages.intended_audience: South Korean IT and enterprise AI adoption leads, software developers, and AI business strategists

pages.title: [Neglected SW Part 1] SW Disappears from the Budget... Concerns over National Competitiveness
pages.what_its_about: Concerns over weakening national competitiveness are emerging as the government significantly increases next year's AI budget while cutting funding for the software (SW) industry, which serves as the core foundation for AI.
key_points: The Ministry of Science and ICT's AI budget for 2027 reached 9.4211 trillion won, up 84.3% year-on-year, but the non-R&D SW budget fell by approximately 40 billion won to around 290 billion won.

Budgets for major SW projects—such as expanding SW infrastructure, supporting public SaaS development and transition, and strengthening overseas expansion capabilities—have been drastically cut, and university support is shifting its focus from SW to AI.

Industry and academia emphasize that for AI technology to be applied to real-world industrial sites and create value, support from traditional software ecosystems such as ERP, DB, and embedded SW is essential.
notable_data_or_quotes: Out of the Ministry of Science and ICT's 29.6476 trillion won budget, 9.4211 trillion won was allocated to the AI sector. This represents an 84.3% increase from this year's 5.0938 trillion won, accounting for 31.8% of the ministry's total budget.
Next year's software-related budget in the non-R&D sector stands at around 290 billion won, down by approximately 40 billion won from about 330 billion won this year.

Eo Yun-ho, President of the Korea Commercial AI Software Association: 'GPUs are ultimately infrastructure, and models are foundational technologies... It is ultimately software that applies that technology to actual business operations, increases productivity, and turns it into services that customers pay for.'

Kim Sook-kyung, Professor at KAIST: 'Simply possessing frontier models does not make a country one of the top three AI powerhouses... Existing industrial ecosystems and enterprises must exist for AI to be built on top of them.'
pages.intended_audience: IT and software industry professionals, government policymakers, AI industry stakeholders

pages.title: 'AI for Everyone' Transforms Daily Life: What Changes Can We Expect?
pages.what_its_about: Introduces real-world applications of daily life AI technologies addressing everyday problems such as shopping, travel, and caregiving, along with the 'AI Festa 26' event showcasing them and the government's 'AI for Everyone' policy.
key_points: 'AI Festa 26' will be held from October 6 to 8 at COEX in Seoul, showcasing AI technologies and use cases that have expanded into everyday life.

A wide range of everyday lifestyle services will be introduced, including Buzzni's shopping AI, Yanolja's travel solutions, Sigonggan's shopping support for the visually impaired, and Zeroweb's senior care.

Under the government's 'AI for Everyone' policy, a consortium comprising SK Telecom, Kakao, and KT plans to launch a nationwide AI service supporting hospital reservations and public service applications in December, following a beta launch this month.

Nationwide tangible AI service: Targeting an official service launch in December following a beta release this month
